## Can I hide orders from specific users?

**FAQ key:** `user_hide_accounts`

Yes. On a computer or tablet, every order in the orderbook has a small hide button (it isn't shown on narrow phone screens). Click it and confirm, and you won't see that account's orders any more — your chats with them are hidden too. They are never told.

When you are signed in, your hidden list is saved with your account settings, encrypted so only you can read it. It follows you when you sign in on another device or another Morphit site.

To undo it, go to **Settings → Hidden accounts** and unhide one person, or everyone at once. When the orderbook has hidden orders, a note at the top says how many, with a **Show anyway** button to peek without unhiding.

Hiding only changes what *you* see. It doesn't ban anyone: their orders still exist, and everyone else still sees them.

---

## How does Morphit's reputation system work?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_reputation`

After a trade, each side can rate the other from 1 to 5 stars and add a short comment — once per order. Reviews are saved on the Blurt blockchain, so they are public and permanent. Nobody, not even the site, can edit or delete them.

Each trader's profile shows their reviews, a star breakdown and a **reputation score from 0 to 5** (for example 4.06). The same score sits on their orders, next to how many trades they have completed.

How the score works, in plain words:

• Newer reviews count more. A review loses half its weight each year.
• A trader with only a few reviews stays close to a neutral 3.0, so one glowing review can't make a stranger look like a veteran.
• A long, recent, good record earns a small bonus. Lots of trading can never rescue bad ratings.
• Only reviews from a real trade partner count. Fake-looking patterns are left out.

**Your reputation is everything.** Morphit has no escrow and no referee. Your track record is what lets a stranger trust you, so treat every trade as if it matters — it does.

---

## How do I build a high reputation score on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `how_to_build_high_reputation`

There's no shortcut: real trades, done well, over time.

**What raises your score**

• **Finish real trades and get reviewed.** A review only counts if it comes from someone you really chatted with (at least 2 messages each way, over at least 15 minutes) and names an order you two traded on whose listing fee was paid.
• **Stay active.** Newer reviews count more — each review loses half its weight per year. The small bonus for a good record also halves for every 6 months without a new review.
• **Be good on both sides.** Your profile shows your rating as a buyer and as a seller separately.
• **Review back.** When a trade goes well, leave your partner an honest review too.

**What doesn't work**

• Reviewing yourself — it's rejected.
• Fake accounts, two friends swapping 5-star reviews, one account aiming most of its reviews at one person, or a group piling bad reviews on someone. These patterns are flagged and left out.
• Lots of reviews from one person — only their latest review of you counts.
• Reviews that don't name a trade. They show on your profile but don't count.

New accounts carry a 🌱 badge until they have 4 completed trades. That's normal — start small.

Anyone can check your score: each site publishes a public reputation receipt (for the technically curious: `/v1/accounts/<name>/reputation-receipt`) that lists every review about you, whether it counted, and why not if it didn't.

---

## How do I leave feedback after a trade?

**FAQ key:** `how_to_leave_feedback`

When the trade is done, you can review the other person from two places:

• **In the chat** for that order. After a payment has been marked as sent, a **Mark this trade complete** card appears under the messages.
• **In [My Orders](/my/orders)**, for orders you posted. Click **Mark complete / review** and pick who you traded with.

Choose 1 to 5 stars, add a comment if you like (up to 256 characters), and submit. If it's your own order, this also marks it complete and takes it off the orderbook.

You can only review someone you really talked with: at least 2 messages each way, spread over at least 15 minutes. The review is signed with your posting key, so there's no password prompt. Morphit charges nothing for it; Blurt takes its usual tiny network fee from your liquid BLURT. It shows on their profile in about a minute.

---

## Can I respond to a review someone left about me?

**FAQ key:** `feedback_reply`

Yes. Open your own profile, find the review under **Reviews received**, and click **Reply**. You get one public reply per review (up to 256 characters). It shows right under the review, so readers see both sides.

Replies are saved on the blockchain like reviews, so they're permanent. Use them to explain calmly, not to argue. Nobody can edit or delete the original review — not you, not the site.

---

## Who can see the reviews I've left for other traders?

**FAQ key:** `reviews_given_visibility`

Everyone. Every profile has a **Reviews given** tab listing each review that person has left, with a link to the order it was about.

That's on purpose: how you rate others is part of your own reputation. If someone hands out 1-star reviews that nobody else agrees with, readers can see the pattern and judge for themselves.

---

## Why did Morphit warn me about a private key in my message?

**FAQ key:** `private_key_warning`

Because it spotted something that looks like a private key or a seed phrase. Morphit checks what you type in chat messages, order terms, review comments and replies to reviews for:

• private keys in the common 'WIF' format (like your Blurt posting or active key),
• 64-character hex keys (such as Monero private keys),
• 12 or more seed-phrase words in a row.

A match turns red, and a warning pops up before anything is sent. A private key is the key to a wallet: whoever sees it can take everything in it, forever. No real support person, admin or trade partner will ever ask for one.

If you choose **Send truncated anyway**, Morphit shortens the key on your device to its first 6 and last 4 characters, so the full secret never leaves. Other order fields and your profile get the same shortening automatically, without the pop-up.

---

## What does the 'New trader' label mean?

**FAQ key:** `new_trader_badge`

It's the little 🌱 sprout next to a trader's name. It means the account has fewer than 4 completed trades on record — counting only orders whose listing fee was paid (plus a trader's free first order), and leaving out trades between accounts flagged as working together.

They might be brand new, or just someone who rarely trades. It isn't a red flag — everyone starts here. If you trade with a newcomer, start with a small amount. Afterwards, an honest review helps the next person decide.

---

## What's on a user's profile page?

**FAQ key:** `profile_pages`

Every profile lives at /@username, and anyone can view it without signing in. From top to bottom:

• **Who they are** — their picture (or a pattern made from their account name), display name, a short bio, and links to their Nostr, website or streaming page if they added any.
• **Reputation** — their 0–5 score, number of ratings, average stars, a 5-to-1 star breakdown, separate buyer and seller ratings, and when they last traded.
• **Tabs** — *Reviews received* (with any replies), *Reviews given*, and *Active orders*, oldest first so the ones closest to expiring come first.

---

## What changes when I'm viewing my own profile vs someone else's?

**FAQ key:** `profile_own_vs_others`

On your own profile you also see:

• your balance card,
• a **Trade history** tab with your completed trades,
• a **Reply** button under each review you haven't answered yet.

On someone else's profile you see a **Message @name** button instead.

Order pages work the same way. On your own order you get **Edit** (only in the first 15 minutes after posting) and **Cancel this order** — or **Re-list this order** once it has expired or been cancelled. On someone else's live order you see the **Message @name** button, with a short note about using it to agree on payment.

---

## Can I share a link to my order?

**FAQ key:** `share_order_link`

Yes. Open the order and copy the address from your browser's address bar — it ends in /@username/ followed by the order's code (like order-k3x9…). Anyone can open it without signing in and see the full offer: price, payment methods, location, terms, and who posted it with their reputation.

Share it anywhere — Nostr, a chat, a forum. The link stays the same if you edit the order. Once the order is completed, cancelled or expired, the link still opens and simply shows that status.

---

## Does Morphit chat have forward secrecy?

**FAQ key:** `forward_secrecy`

No. Morphit chat does not have forward secrecy. That's a deliberate trade-off — here's the honest version.

**How a message is locked.** Each message gets a fresh one-time key, mixed with your chat key and your partner's. Only the two of you can open it, and your partner can tell it really came from you. Your chat key is made from your Blurt posting key and stays the same until that key changes.

**If a key is ever stolen.** Anyone who later gets your partner's chat key can read every message ever sent to them. By default you keep a copy of what you send, so your own key opens those too. You can stop keeping that copy (⋮ → Chat Security), but your partner's key still opens them, and the encrypted messages stay on the chain forever.

**Why we chose this.**

• Any message opens on its own — out of order, years later, on a new device — with no setup and nothing to pair.
• Every device signed in to your account is the same chat identity.
• The crypto code stays small and easy to audit.
• Someone holding your posting key can already post, chat and publish a new chat key as you, so per-message keys would protect little.

**If that's not enough for you** — for talks that could be investigated years from now — use a dedicated messenger such as Matrix/Element, Session or Signal. Morphit chat is for arranging a trade.

---

## If I disagree with my counterparty later, can I prove what we agreed to in chat?

**FAQ key:** `chat_dispute_recourse`

Partly. Morphit chat is stored on the Blurt blockchain, so nobody can edit or quietly delete what was said, and you can scroll back to the very first message. (If you stopped keeping your own copy in ⋮ → Chat Security, you can't reread your own messages after you leave — your partner still can.)

**What you can show others.** Each message is a blockchain transaction signed by the sender's account, with a time and a transaction ID. Anyone can look these up on a Blurt block explorer to confirm *who* sent a message to *whom* and *when*. The chain holds only the encrypted form, so it can't prove the *wording* to an outsider.

**Export.** Open the chat's ⋮ menu and choose **Export chat**. You get a PDF of every message the two of you ever exchanged, in every chat about every order, each with its UTC time and transaction ID, plus a page explaining how to check them. It's an ordinary, editable file — a tidy record for a mediator or court, not proof of the wording on its own.

**What it can't do.** Morphit has no escrow and nobody who settles disputes, so evidence can't force anyone to pay — see 'Why no Escrow or Arbitration service?'. How much weight a court or mediator gives it depends on where you are.

**Tip:** before anyone sends money, write the exact asset, amount, payment method and any special terms in the chat.

---

## What's public and what's private about my trades on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `chat_vs_feedback_visibility`

Some of it is private and some is public — on purpose.

**Private (only you and your trade partner can read it):**

• **What you say in chat** — prices, payment details, addresses, meeting places, phone numbers. Messages are end-to-end encrypted; operators and anyone watching the blockchain see only scrambled text. See 'Are my chats private?'.

**Public (anyone can read it):**

• **Your orders**, including prices and terms.
• **Reviews** — stars, comments and replies. Each review names the order it's about, so it publicly links the two accounts (@squirrel and @scooby) to that trade. See 'Who can see the reviews I've left for other traders?'.
• **Everything about a chat except the words:** who talked to whom, when, about which order, roughly how long each message was, and how far each of you has read (read receipts).

All of it is saved on the Blurt blockchain, and nothing saved there can be deleted. The only difference is who can read it.

Why? Chat stays private so payment details don't leak. Reviews stay public so anyone can check a reputation. If even the fact that you talked must stay hidden, use a separate secure messenger for that part.

---

## How does Morphit protect me from scammers and stop them from getting my private keys or personal info?

**FAQ key:** `how_morphit_protects_me`

Mostly by having little worth stealing, plus a few safety nets.

**Little to steal.** Morphit never holds your coins, and your private keys are made on your device and never sent to the site. No email, phone number or ID is asked for, and IP addresses are kept only in memory, to limit abuse. A hacked server holds none of your keys and no identities — though it could serve tampered page code, so use sites you trust.

**Key guard.** Paste something that looks like a private key or seed phrase into a chat, order or review and you get a red warning; send anyway and only its first 6 and last 4 characters go out. See 'Why did Morphit warn me about a private key in my message?'.

**Spam gates.** A stranger who isn't answering one of your orders must pay a small BLURT fee to message you first, unless you wrote to them first. Blocked accounts can't reach you. See 'How does Morphit stop spam and unsolicited messages from strangers?'.

**Hard-to-fake reviews.** A review counts only if the reviewer really chatted with you and names an order one of you paid a listing fee for — and only their latest review of you counts. See 'How does Morphit stop fake reviews?'.

**A locked-down site.** What you send is checked, and pages run only the site's own code. See 'Is Morphit vulnerable to hacking, data theft, or takedowns?'.

No software can stop a scammer talking you into a bad deal — see 'What scams should I watch out for on Morphit?'.

---

## How does Morphit stop spam and unsolicited messages from strangers?

**FAQ key:** `chat_anti_spam`

Three layers keep strangers from flooding you, while normal trade chat stays free.

**1. Block.** You can block any account; its messages to you are then simply not delivered. A new account still has to get past the two layers below.

**2. A small first-contact fee.** The first message to someone you have never chatted with costs 5 BLURT, paid once per person (90% to the site operator, 10% to the Morphit treasury). It is free if the two of you have already exchanged a message, or if you are writing about one of their live orders — posting an order is an invitation.

The fee doubles for each extra stranger a sender contacts within 5 minutes: 5, 10, 20, 40… up to 640 BLURT each. Eight strangers in 5 minutes cost 1,275 BLURT. After 5 quiet minutes it is back to 5.

**3. Limits until you reply.** Until you answer someone, they can send you at most 50 messages, and at most 20 unanswered new people can start chats with you in 24 hours. Your first reply lifts both limits for that person.

These numbers are fixed in the code and the same on every Morphit site; operators can't change them.

---

## How does the chat inbox work? Can I mute or unmute someone?

**FAQ key:** `chat_inbox_features`

Tap **Chat** in the header to open your inbox. It works like email: **one card per discussion**, not one per person.

Talk with the same trader about three orders and you get three cards. Each card has a "RE:" line naming the order and its state — Live, Canceled, Expired or Paid — or "RE: -" if the chat isn't about an order.

Opening a card marks **only that one** read, on all your devices. Unread cards have a green border, and the badge on your avatar (top right), the browser tab and the site icon show the unread count. **Mark all as read** clears them all. Read marks are saved publicly on the chain: anyone can see up to when you read a chat with someone, never what it said.

Three tabs:
• **Inbox** — everything lands here.
• **Starred** — tap the star on a card (or in the conversation's ⋮ menu) to keep it here; tap again to move it back.
• **Archived** — tap **Archive** to file a discussion away; it stops counting as unread, and a new message brings it back. **Restore** returns it to the Inbox.

Starred and Archived sync between your devices, encrypted; the other person never sees them.

**Mute = Block.** In a conversation, open ⋮ → Block: that account can no longer message you. To unmute, go to **Settings → Blocked accounts** and tap Unblock. Blocks are public — see 'If I block someone, will they know?'.

---

## How does Morphit let me know when something happens — a new message, an order filling, feedback arriving?

**FAQ key:** `notifications_overview`

Morphit tells you about new things in a few ways. The quiet ones are always on; the louder ones are your choice, in **Settings → Notifications**.

**Always on (no permission needed):**
• The browser tab title starts with the unread count, like "(3)".
• The site icon in the tab gets a small dot with the count.
• If you installed Morphit as an app, its icon gets a badge (where your system supports it).
These work while you are signed in and unlocked.

**Your choice (off until you turn them on):**
• **Desktop notifications** — a pop-up when the Morphit tab isn't in front. Your browser asks permission the first time one would show.
• **Sound** — a short chime.
• **Vibration** — a short buzz, on phones that support it.
• **Push notifications** — alerts even when Morphit is closed. They travel through your browser maker's push service; see 'How do push notifications work with my privacy?'.

**What you're told about:** orders and trade steps, chat messages, and feedback. All three are on by default; switch off any you don't want.

**Quiet hours** and **Silence everything** stop pop-ups and sounds. Push notifications still appear (browsers require it), but silently.

For the chat inbox, see "How does the chat inbox work? Can I mute or unmute someone?".

---

## What does "We couldn't safely send" mean?

**FAQ key:** `chat_key_changed`

The first time you message someone, Morphit remembers their chat key in your browser. Before every later message it checks that the key your site reports still matches. If something doesn't add up, the message is held back instead of sent.

**Most common: their key changed.** That happens when your partner resets their keys — or when someone is trying to read your messages. Open ⋮ → **Verify peer** and compare the safety number with them another way (a call, in person). Accept the new key only if the numbers match; until then nothing is sent. Their older messages stay readable but are marked unverified.

**Other cases** — the key record looks tampered with, is older than one you've already seen, is missing on the chain, or is garbled. These point to a broken or out-of-date indexer, not to your partner.

**What to do:**
• Retry once — it may be a hiccup.
• Switch to another Morphit site (link at the bottom of the page); each runs its own indexer.
• Ask your partner, another way, whether they reset their keys.

These checks read the chain through your site's own servers, so they catch a broken indexer, not a lying operator. The safety number protects you there: compare it once with each partner.

See also 'How does Morphit chat work?' and 'Are my chats private?'.

---

## My order isn't showing up. What does the fee status mean?

**FAQ key:** `order_fee_rejected`

An order shows on the public orderbook only after its listing fee is confirmed. **My orders** shows each order's fee status:

• **Visible in orderbook** — fee confirmed. All done.
• **Verified (attested)** — a BTC or XMR fee the block explorers couldn't answer for, vouched for by two independent community members instead. Your order is live.
• **Awaiting attestation** — a BTC or XMR fee still being checked. A paid fee is usually confirmed within minutes of your payment confirming on its own chain.
• **Waiting for your BTC fee** — pay the BTC fee to the address shown for that order; it goes live once the payment confirms.
• **Not yet verified** — not checked yet. Wait a little.
• **Fee payment not received** — no matching fee was found: the payment failed, went to the wrong place, or the transaction ID was wrong.
• **Fee underpaid** — the fee was too small. A BLURT fee goes up when you have many live orders or posted many in the last 24 hours.
• **Payment already used** — that BTC or XMR payment already paid for another order. One payment pays for one order.
• **Fee can't be checked** — post the XMR order again, this time with the transaction key.

If an order is stuck on a "Not in orderbook" status, cancel it and post a new one with the right fee.

---

## Signup isn't working. What do these errors mean?

**FAQ key:** `signup_stuck`

This site's relay creates your Blurt account and pays the fee for you (about 102 BLURT), so it has limits against abuse. What the messages mean:

• **"Verifying you're human…" takes long, or "Human verification failed"** — your browser solves a small puzzle (Altcha). Close other tabs, refresh and try again.
• **"You've made too many attempts. Try again in an hour."** — too many sign-up tries from your internet connection in the last hour. Shared Wi-Fi counts everyone on it. Wait, or use another network.
• **"You recently created an account. Please wait…"** — signups from one connection must be spaced apart (an hour, by default).
• **"You've reached today's signup limit"** — your connection's daily limit. Try tomorrow.
• **"This instance has reached its daily signup limit"** — the whole site's daily cap. It resets at midnight UTC, or try another Morphit site.
• **"Signups are temporarily unavailable"**, **"temporarily out of funds"** or **"Registration is paused"** — the operator has paused signups or needs to top up the relay. Try later, or another site.
• **"Your signup token expired or was already used"** — often your connection changed (say, Wi-Fi to mobile data). Refresh and retry.
• **"That name was just taken"**, **"isn't allowed"** or **"is reserved"** — pick another name. Names are 3–16 characters: lowercase letters, digits and single dashes, starting with a letter, no dots.
• **"Registration was rejected"** — try a different name.
• **"The Blurt network did not confirm in time"** — wait a minute and retry with the same name.

See also 'What do I need to sign up?', and after signing up, 'What is the welcome bonus and how do I earn it?'.

---

## What is the "Verified chat" badge on a review?

**FAQ key:** `verified_chat_badge`

A small green check on a review. It means the reviewer and the trader really talked in chat before the review was posted:
• at least 2 messages from each side,
• spread over at least 15 minutes,
• and the two haven't been caught swapping top reviews with each other.

Today every new review needs this — a review without such a chat is refused — so all new reviews carry the badge. Some older reviews don't.

**What it doesn't prove:** that the two accounts are different people. One patient person with two accounts can chat with themselves.

**Why not check IP addresses?** That would mean collecting them, VPNs and Tor would beat it, and honest people on shared Wi-Fi would be wrongly flagged.

**How to use it:** as one clue among several. A reviewer with an older account who has reviewed many different traders tells you more than the badge alone.

---

## Why are some reviews greyed out as 'not counted toward rating'?

**FAQ key:** `feedback_suppressed`

These suppressed reviews still show, but they don't count toward the star rating or review count at the top of the profile. They're greyed out and marked "Not counted toward the rating".

A review doesn't count when:
• **Same maker:** both accounts were created by the same account (not a Morphit site's signup service) and became active within 5 minutes of each other.
• **Back-scratching:** two accounts gave each other 3 or more top reviews (4.8★+ on average) within 7 days and reviewed nobody else.
• **Pile-on:** 3 or more accounts left low reviews (2★ or less on average) for one trader within 7 days, and those accounts started around the same time and review almost no one else.
• **One favourite:** at least 80% of a reviewer's reviews (5 or more in 30 days), averaging 4.5★+, go to one trader.
• It isn't linked to an order, so it can't be tied to a trade.
• The same reviewer reviewed this trader again later — only their latest review counts.

**Why show them at all?** The chain is public, so hiding them would only pretend. Greyed out says: this exists, but it doesn't count.

**Wrongly flagged?** The checks aren't perfect. The operator of the site you're viewing can clear a flag for a pair — contact them.

See also "How does Morphit's reputation system work?".

---

## If I block someone, will they know?

**FAQ key:** `block_privacy`

**Morphit never tells someone you blocked them** — telling a stalker who blocked them only helps them get around it. But a block isn't secret.

**What they see:** if they message you, their message shows as not accepted for delivery ("the recipient may not be taking messages from you right now"), without saying why.

**What's public:** a block is saved on the Blurt chain, like everything on Morphit. Anyone who reads the chain — or looks up your block list through a site's public data feed — can see whom you blocked and when. Morphit's screens just don't point it out.

**If they make a new account:** your block covers only the account you blocked. A new one must pay the first-contact fee (5 BLURT and up, doubling if they rush) — unless they write about one of your live orders, which is free. Also, at most 20 unanswered new people can start chats with you per 24 hours. You can block the new account too.

**Changed your mind?** Go to **Settings → Blocked accounts** and tap Unblock. That's public too, and messages sent while they were blocked are not delivered later.

See also "How does Morphit stop spam and unsolicited messages from strangers?".

---

## What is Mana on Blurt?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_mana`

On Blurt, Mana is your voting power. It only decides how much weight your upvotes carry. Think of a stamina bar: each vote uses a little, and it refills by about 20% a day. The more Blurt Power (BP) you hold, the more your votes count.

Mana does **not** pay for anything you do. (On Steem and Hive, "Resource Credits" pay for actions; Blurt dropped that.) On Blurt, every action costs a small fee in BLURT, taken from your liquid (unstaked) balance: a transfer, a post, and on Morphit an order, a review or an encrypted chat message. Mana only matters for voting.

So the rule is simple: keep a little liquid BLURT in your account and your actions go through. You never have to wait for Mana to refill before you trade. Receiving BLURT is free, so topping up is easy.

---

## What are the minimum hardware requirements to run a Morphit node?

**FAQ key:** `node_minimum_requirements`

Modest. An old PC or laptop, a small mini-PC, a cheap rented server (VPS) or a Raspberry Pi will do, as long as it meets these minimums:

• **CPU:** 2 cores or more (64-bit x86 or ARM).
• **Memory:** 4 GB of RAM or more.
• **Disk:** 80 GB free or more. An SSD is best.
• **System:** Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, or a flavor built on it (Linux Mint 22, Pop!_OS 24.04, Zorin OS 17). The one-command installer refuses anything else, including Debian and older Ubuntu.
• **Power and internet:** a machine that stays on.

The installer checks your machine before it starts and tells you if anything falls short.

**What you don't need:**

• Your own blockchain node. Morphit reads the Blurt network through public servers.
• A static IP. At home, the installer keeps your domain pointed at you even when your address changes (dynamic DNS).
• A domain, if you choose Tor-only. Your site then lives at a `.onion` address.
• A data center. But a normal (clearnet) site run from home will expose your home IP address to every visitor. A Tor-only site does not.

One cost to know: your relay pays about 102 BLURT for every account it creates, so a site that signs up many people can lose money if very few people on it are actually trading.

---

## Can I use Morphit on my iPhone or iPad?

**FAQ key:** `iphone_install`

Yes. Morphit is a web app (a PWA), so there is nothing to get from the App Store and no jailbreak.

To put it on your Home Screen:
1. Open this site in **Safari**.
2. Tap **Share** (the square with an arrow pointing up).
3. Tap **Add to Home Screen**.
4. Tap **Add**.

The new icon opens Morphit full screen, like an app. Notifications on iPhone and iPad need iOS 16.4 or newer, and work only from the Home Screen icon.

---

## Is there a block explorer for Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `block_explorer`

Yes. Go to [the explorer](/explorer) to look up any Blurt account, transaction or block. It is public and needs no account. Morphit's own actions (orders, reviews, chat messages, which stay encrypted, and more) are labelled in plain words, so you can tell what each one is.

Payments in other coins happen on their own blockchains. When a transaction ID for one of them appears in a chat, Morphit links it to an outside explorer for that coin, for example mempool.space for Bitcoin and xmrchain.net for Monero. The site's operator can change these links.

---

## Can I build a block explorer or aggregator on top of Morphit's data?

**FAQ key:** `public_api`

Yes, and it is free. Every Morphit instance serves the same read-only public API under `/v1/*`: no API key, no signup. Only the hostname changes.

• **Reference:** `docs/API.md` in the source lists every endpoint, for example `/v1/orderbook` (live updates at `/v1/orderbook/stream`), `/v1/orders/:account`, `/v1/accounts/:account/feedback`, `/v1/instances` and `/v1/health`. RSS, Atom and JSON feeds live under `/rss/orderbook`.
• **Stability:** documented `/v1` fields are never renamed or removed without a new `/v2`. New fields can appear, so ignore ones you don't know.
• **Rate limits:** by default 120 requests a minute per IP for lists and 600 for single-record lookups. Each operator can change these. Going over returns `429` with a `Retry-After` header.
• **Writing:** the API doesn't change data. Orders, reviews and chat are Blurt transactions you sign yourself; an instance only passes a signed transaction on (`POST /v1/broadcast`).
• **Chat:** messages are on-chain but encrypted. Only the two people in the chat can read them.

For heavy use, run your own instance (see `RUN-A-MORPHIT-NODE.md`): no rate limits, and no dependence on someone else's server. Use `/v1/instances` to find other instances and spread your load.

All of this data is on the public Blurt chain anyway. The API just saves you from building your own indexer.

---

## What is the featured slot and how does the auction work?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_featured_slot`

Featured slots put up to **3** orders in a highlighted spot at the top of the orderbook and on the home page of **this site**. Each site runs its own, so a bid here only buys space here.

**How to bid.** In [My orders](/my/orders), pick one of your live orders whose listing fee is confirmed, and choose 6, 24 or 72 hours. You pay the site's hourly price times the hours, in BLURT. Each operator sets their own price, and the form shows the total before you pay. 90% goes to the site's operator and 10% to the Morphit treasury.

**Who gets the slots.** Bids rank by BLURT paid per hour; at the same rate, the earlier bid wins. Because the form pays the site's current price, slots usually go first come, first served. If all 3 are taken, your bid waits and shows when a slot frees up. Your hours start counting as soon as the bid is recorded, even while it waits. To push someone out, a bid must pay at least 1 BLURT an hour or 5% more than them, whichever is bigger; the form checks this before you pay.

**No refunds.** The BLURT goes out with the bid and is not returned. See 'What happens to my featured slot if someone outbids me?'

---

## What happens to my featured slot if someone outbids me?

**FAQ key:** `featured_slot_displaced`

Your bid stays on record, but it drops out of view. Nothing is refunded.

Morphit shows the 3 bids paying the most BLURT per hour. If a new bid beats the lowest of the 3 by at least 1 BLURT an hour or 5% (whichever is bigger), that lowest bid drops to 4th place and leaves the featured spot. If a bid above yours ends while your hours are still running, yours comes back. Your hours keep counting the whole time: you paid for a chance at the slot during those hours, not for guaranteed visibility.

**What helps:**

• **Outbid alerts.** If you turned on push notifications, Morphit tells you when you're pushed out, with a link to the order in My orders. My orders also marks the bid "Outranked".
• **No last-second sniping.** When a new bid comes in and a top-3 bid ends within 5 minutes, that bid gets 5 more minutes. This can happen up to 6 times per bid (30 minutes in all), so you have time to respond.
• **Look first.** Before bidding, check what the current slots pay, and prefer shorter bids when competition is high.

---

## How can I be sure no one is reading my chats? (Verify safety number)

**FAQ key:** `verify_peer_fingerprint`

Morphit chats are end-to-end encrypted: messages are locked on your device, and only you and your partner can open them.

There is one weak spot. The first time you chat with someone, your browser trusts the chat key your site's server says is theirs. A dishonest server could slip in its own key and read along. **The safety number lets you rule that out.** If your partner's key changes later, nothing is sent to the new key until you check the new number and accept it (see 'What does "We couldn't safely send" mean?').

**How to check:**
1. Open the chat and tap ⋮ → **Verify peer**.
2. You see 60 digits in 12 groups of 5. Your partner opens the same screen.
3. Compare the digits by voice call, in person, or another channel you both already trust. **Not in this chat.**
4. If every digit matches, nobody swapped a key. If even one differs, treat the chat as compromised and stop.

**What it can't catch:** the wrong person on the call (you must recognise them), a hacked phone, or a dishonest copy of the app itself.

Checking is optional and posts nothing to the chain. The number is made from public keys only, and faking a match is far out of reach.

---

## What is QR login and is it safe?

**FAQ key:** `qr_login`

QR login signs you in to Morphit on a computer using your phone, without typing your seed phrase.

**How it works:** on the computer, choose **Sign in with your phone via QR**. A one-time code appears; it works for 5 minutes. On your phone (signed in and unlocked), tap your avatar → **Sign in to another device** and scan the code. Your phone shows the website's address. Tap **Yes, that was me** only if you just opened that site yourself.

**Why it's safe:** your keys never leave your phone. The code is only a request, so a screenshot of it is useless without your phone saying yes. The server just passes along a sealed message it can't read or fake.

**Watch out:** read the website address on your phone carefully. A fake site can look almost the same (a 1 instead of an l). If you didn't just open it, tap **No, I didn't**.

**Good to know:** the computer is read-only. You can browse and see your orders and profile there, but to post, send messages, leave reviews or read encrypted chats, use your phone. If you lose your phone, sign in with your written seed phrase.

---

## What is USDT (Tether)?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_usdt`

USDT (Tether) is a stablecoin: a crypto token made to stay worth about 1 US dollar. It is issued by the company Tether. People use it to hold dollar value without leaving crypto.

On Morphit you can buy and sell USDT person to person on four networks: Ethereum (ERC-20), Tron (TRC-20), Solana (SPL) and BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20). You must pick the network for every trade; see 'Which USDT network should I pick — ERC-20, TRC-20, SPL, or BEP-20?'

USDT is for trading only. You can't pay Morphit's fees with it: listing fees are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR, and first-message and featured-slot fees in BLURT.

---

## What is USDC?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_usdc`

USDC (USD Coin) is a stablecoin: a crypto token made to stay worth about 1 US dollar. It is issued by the company Circle.

On Morphit you can buy and sell USDC person to person on four networks: Ethereum (ERC-20), Solana (SPL), Base and Polygon. Pick one that both you and your trading partner use. The order form makes you choose, because coins sent on the wrong network can be lost.

USDC is for trading only: Morphit's fees are never paid in USDC. For the honest privacy trade-offs, see [the USDC privacy guide](/privacy/usdc).

---

## Why does Morphit show a chip about how USDT is issued and transmitted?

**FAQ key:** `why_usdt_warning`

Morphit shows this chip to share two facts, so you can choose with open eyes:

• **Tether can freeze addresses.** Tether, the company behind USDT, can freeze the USDT at an address, and has done so.
• **USDT payments are public.** On all four networks (Ethereum, Tron, Solana, BNB Smart Chain) anyone can see the transactions. That's how those chains work, not something special about USDT.

This doesn't make USDT bad: it holds a steady dollar value and is easy to trade almost anywhere. If privacy matters most, XMR is the better tool. If you want a coin no company can freeze, look at BTC, BLURT, BCH, LTC, DASH, DOGE, DCR, SOL, ETH, or XRP. The chip is information, not a verdict.

---

## Why does Morphit show a privacy warning when I trade USDC?

**FAQ key:** `why_usdc_warning`

For the same reason as USDT: USDC is a stablecoin run by a company. The warning shares two facts:

• **Circle can freeze addresses.** Circle, the company behind USDC, can freeze the USDC at an address on any supported network, and has done so.
• **USDC payments are public** on all four networks (Ethereum, Solana, Base, Polygon).

The other coins here (XMR, BTC, BLURT, BCH, LTC, DASH, DOGE, ZEC, ARRR, DCR, SOL, ETH, XRP) have no company that can freeze them.

Many traders accept this trade-off for a steady dollar value, and that's fine. The warning appears on Morphit's order form and in the window where you share an address; it never blocks anything, it just makes sure the choice is yours. An operator can also switch USDC off for their whole site. If so, pick another coin or another site.

---

## Which USDT network should I pick — ERC-20, TRC-20, SPL, or BEP-20?

**FAQ key:** `which_usdt_network`

Pick a network that you and your trading partner both use. Rough fees, as shown in the order form:

• **Tron (TRC-20):** about $1, fast. The most common for person-to-person trades.
• **Ethereum (ERC-20):** about $5–20, slow. Accepted almost everywhere.
• **Solana (SPL):** under $0.01, fast. Needs a Solana wallet on both sides.
• **BNB Smart Chain (BEP-20):** about $0.30, fast, less common.

There is **no default** on Morphit: the order form won't post a USDT order until you choose. That's on purpose, because USDT sent on the wrong network can be lost for good. Take extra care with Ethereum and BNB Smart Chain: their addresses look the same (both start with `0x`). Before you send, check the network named next to the address in the chat.

---

## Which USDC network should I use?

**FAQ key:** `which_usdc_network`

Pick a network that you and your trading partner both use. Rough fees, as shown in the order form:

• **Solana (SPL):** under $0.01, fast. Needs a Solana wallet on both sides.
• **Base:** about $0.01, fast. Works with Ethereum-style wallets.
• **Polygon:** about $0.01, fast. Also works with Ethereum-style wallets.
• **Ethereum (ERC-20):** about $5–20, slow. Accepted almost everywhere, but costly for small trades.

**Watch out:** Ethereum, Base and Polygon addresses look exactly the same (they all start with `0x`), but each network keeps its own separate balance. If you send USDC on Polygon to an address your partner gave you for Base, it lands on Polygon and their Base wallet won't show it. The order form makes you choose a network, and a shared address in the chat says which network to send on. Always check it before you send.

---

## What is DAI?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_dai`

DAI is a stablecoin: a coin meant to stay worth about one US dollar. It is run by MakerDAO, not by a single company like Tether (USDT) or Circle (USDC).

• **No freeze button.** The DAI token itself gives nobody a way to freeze your address.
• **Partly backed by USDC.** Some of what keeps DAI at $1 is USDC, which Circle *can* freeze. So DAI is more independent than USDT or USDC, but not fully.
• **Not private.** Every DAI payment is public on its blockchain.

On Morphit you can trade DAI on four networks: Ethereum, Polygon, Base and Arbitrum One. You pick one when you post, and both of you must use that same network (see "Which DAI network should I use?").

You can't pay listing fees in DAI — those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR. More tips: [DAI privacy guide](/privacy/dai).

---

## Why does Morphit show a privacy warning when I trade DAI?

**FAQ key:** `why_dai_warning`

Because DAI is only partly independent, and never private. The warning says three things:

• **No freeze button on DAI itself.** Unlike USDT and USDC, nobody can block your address on the DAI token. That is a real plus.
• **Some backing is USDC.** Part of what keeps DAI at $1 is USDC, and Circle can freeze USDC. So Circle's power reaches DAI indirectly.
• **Everything is public.** Anyone can see DAI payments on Ethereum, Polygon, Base and Arbitrum.

The warning is just information — it never stops you from trading. A site's operator can also switch DAI off for their whole site.

---

## Which DAI network should I use?

**FAQ key:** `which_dai_network`

Use a network you and your trade partner both have. Morphit supports DAI on four:

• **Ethereum (ERC-20)** — works almost everywhere, but fees are high (often $5–20 a payment).
• **Polygon** — low fees, usually cents.
• **Base** — Coinbase's network on top of Ethereum; low fees.
• **Arbitrum One** — another network on top of Ethereum; low fees.

**Be careful:** all four use the same kind of address (`0x…`), so an address looks identical on every one. But each network keeps its own separate balance. DAI sent on the wrong network may be lost, or very hard to get back.

You pick the network when you post the order, and the address you share in chat names it too. Still, agree on the network in chat before anyone sends.

---

## How does arbitrage between Morphit and centralized/decentralized exchanges work?

**FAQ key:** `arbitrage_morphit_vs_exchanges`

Morphit keeps arbitrage cheap. Posting an order costs only a small listing fee (about 12.5¢ in BLURT, or 25¢ in BTC or XMR). Replying to someone else's order costs no Morphit fee, just Blurt's tiny network fee. And because Morphit never holds your coins, there are no withdrawal fees, limits or waiting times.

If you see a price gap between Morphit and an exchange (Coinbase, Kraken, Uniswap and so on), post an order on the cheap side. Choose **Market price** and add a small +/- percent: the order then follows the market rate, so you never have to re-price it.

How you settle is up to you and your trade partner: wallet to wallet for crypto-for-crypto, or any payment method you both agree on.

One limit: an account with more than 3 orders live (or posted in the last 24 hours) pays a higher BLURT fee for each extra one — 1.25× for the 4th, 1.56× for the 5th, and rising. It is there to stop spam.

---

## Can I market-make or run a trading bot on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `market_making`

Yes. Morphit welcomes market makers and bots.

• **Low cost.** There's no maker or taker fee. Posting an order costs a small listing fee (about 12.5¢ in BLURT, or 25¢ in BTC or XMR); replying to someone else's order costs no Morphit fee.
• **Orders that price themselves.** Choose **Market price** with a +/- percent, and the order follows the market rate on its own.
• **Open data.** Read the orderbook through the public `/v1` API and its live stream, the RSS feeds or the read-only MCP tools — no API key, no signup, no KYC.
• **Your keys, your coins.** An order is a plain Blurt transaction. Your bot signs and sends it itself; Morphit never holds your funds.

One limit: an account with more than 3 orders live (or posted in the last 24 hours) pays a higher BLURT fee for each extra one — 1.25× for the 4th, 1.56× for the 5th, and rising. A bot that keeps many orders open pays that higher rate when it pays in BLURT; the BTC and XMR fee stays the same.

---

## What is DOGE on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_doge`

DOGE is Dogecoin, one of the best-known coins. Like Bitcoin, every payment is public on its blockchain. No company issues it, and nobody can freeze your coins. It is merge-mined with Litecoin, so the same miners help secure both.

On Morphit, DOGE is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** start with `D` (most common), or with `9` or `A` (rare).

**Privacy:** Dogecoin has no privacy features. Use a fresh receive address for every trade — most wallets make one for you. More tips: [DOGE privacy guide](/privacy/doge).

---

## What is ZEC on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_zec`

ZEC is Zcash. With Zcash you choose, per address, whether payments are public or private:

• **Transparent addresses** (`t1…`, `t3…`) work like Bitcoin: anyone can see who paid whom, and how much.
• **Shielded addresses** (`zs1…`, and the newer `u1…`) keep payments private: when both of you use shielded addresses, the sender, the receiver and the amount are hidden.

Morphit accepts all of these. Agree with your trade partner which kind to use — some older wallets can't send to `u1…` addresses.

On Morphit, ZEC is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR). More tips: [ZEC privacy guide](/privacy/zec).

---

## What is Pirate Chain (ARRR), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_arrr`

Pirate Chain (ARRR) is a coin where **every** payment is private: the sender, the receiver and the amount are always hidden. It has no public (transparent) addresses at all. It is on Morphit so people can trade it person to person, without ID.

On Morphit, ARRR is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** start with `zs1` and are 78 characters long. They look exactly like Zcash addresses, so check that the order says ARRR, and receive with a Pirate Chain wallet.

A site's operator can switch ARRR off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [ARRR privacy guide](/privacy/arrr).

---

## What is Decred (DCR), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_dcr`

Decred (DCR) is secured by both miners and coin holders: miners make each block, and holders with staking "tickets" vote on it. Holders also vote on changes to the rules.

Payments are public by default, like Bitcoin. The Decred wallet has optional mixing (CoinShuffle++) for more privacy.

On Morphit, DCR is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** start with `Ds` (most common) or `Dc`, and are 35 characters long. Use a fresh one for each trade.

A site's operator can switch DCR off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [DCR privacy guide](/privacy/dcr).

---

## What is Solana (SOL), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_sol`

Solana (SOL) is a fast proof-of-stake blockchain: validators who stake SOL take turns making blocks. Nobody can freeze your coins. Every payment is public.

On Morphit, SOL is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** are 32–44 letters and numbers (most are 44). A SOL address looks just like a USDT or USDC address on Solana, so check that the order says SOL.

**Copy and paste addresses — never type them.** Solana addresses have no built-in typo check, so a mistyped one can be a real address nobody owns, and the coins are lost.

Use a fresh address for each trade. A site's operator can switch SOL off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [SOL privacy guide](/privacy/sol).

---

## What is Ethereum (ETH), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_eth`

Ethereum (ETH) is the coin of the Ethereum blockchain, which has run on proof-of-stake since 2022. Nobody can freeze your ETH. Every payment is public.

On Morphit, ETH is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** start with `0x` and are 42 characters long. An ETH address looks exactly like a USDT, USDC or DAI address, so check that the order says ETH. Morphit trades ETH on the main Ethereum network only — not on Base, Arbitrum or Polygon.

**Paste the raw `0x…` address, never type it.** Morphit doesn't accept names like `alice.eth` and doesn't check an address's typo checksum. Also make sure it is a normal wallet address, not a smart contract, which may refuse the ETH.

A site's operator can switch ETH off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [ETH privacy guide](/privacy/eth).

---

## What is Ripple (XRP), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_xrp`

XRP is the coin of the XRP Ledger. There is no mining: a list of trusted validators agrees on each new entry. Nobody can freeze native XRP. Every payment is public.

On Morphit, XRP is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** start with `r` and are 25–35 characters long.

Two things to know before you trade:
• **No destination tags.** Morphit can't pass along a destination tag (the extra number exchanges ask for). So whoever receives the XRP must share their own wallet's address — never an exchange deposit address, or the XRP can land in the exchange's pool and never reach them.
• **1 XRP minimum for a new address.** An XRP address only exists once it holds at least 1 XRP. Sending less to a brand-new address fails, so its first payment must be at least 1 XRP.

A site's operator can switch XRP off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [XRP privacy guide](/privacy/xrp).

---

## What is Bitcoin Cash (BCH), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_bch`

Bitcoin Cash (BCH) is a coin that split off from Bitcoin in 2017. Like Bitcoin, every payment is public, and nobody can freeze your coins.

On Morphit, BCH is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses:** Morphit accepts the modern CashAddr format (`bitcoincash:q…` or `bitcoincash:p…`, with or without the `bitcoincash:` part) and the old format starting with `1` or `3`. Old-format BCH addresses look just like Bitcoin addresses, so check that the order says BCH.

Use a fresh address for each trade; CashFusion (optional mixing in some BCH wallets) can add privacy. A site's operator can switch BCH off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [BCH privacy guide](/privacy/bch).

---

## What is Litecoin (LTC), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_ltc`

Litecoin (LTC) is one of the oldest coins, started in 2011 from Bitcoin's code. Like Bitcoin, payments are public and nobody can freeze your coins.

On Morphit, LTC is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses:** Morphit accepts addresses starting with `L`, `M`, `3` or `ltc1`. An LTC address starting with `3` looks like a Bitcoin address, so check that the order says LTC.

**Privacy:** Litecoin has an optional private mode called MWEB, but MWEB addresses (`ltcmweb1…`) can't be shared on Morphit — you receive LTC at a regular address. Use a fresh one for each trade.

A site's operator can switch LTC off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [LTC privacy guide](/privacy/ltc).

---

## What is Dash (DASH), and why is it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_dash`

Dash (DASH) is a Bitcoin-style coin: payments are public by default, and nobody can freeze your coins. Dash wallets offer optional mixing called PrivateSend for more privacy.

On Morphit, DASH is **trade-only**: you can buy and sell it, but you can't pay listing fees with it (those are paid in BLURT, BTC or XMR).

**Addresses** start with `X` (most common) or `7`, and are 34 characters long. Use a fresh one for each trade.

A site's operator can switch DASH off for their site; other Morphit sites can still trade it. More tips: [DASH privacy guide](/privacy/dash).

---

## I'm a wallet developer — can I integrate Morphit's orderbook into my wallet UI?

**FAQ key:** `wallet_developer_api`

Yes, please. Every Morphit site serves the same free, public, read-only API at `/v1/…` — no API key, no signup. It is documented in `docs/API.md` in the source code.

**What you can build:**
• An orderbook screen filtered to the coins your wallet supports (`/v1/orderbook?asset=…`)
• Live updates without polling (`/v1/orderbook/stream`)
• Trader reputation: rating and feedback count (`/v1/accounts/<name>/feedback`); each orderbook entry also carries the trader's rating and completed trades
• Order details: amounts, payment methods, region, terms

**Good to know:**
• Writing doesn't go through the API. Posting an order or a reply is a Blurt transaction your wallet signs with the user's keys.
• Chat is end-to-end encrypted inside the user's app. Most chat routes are deliberately left out of `docs/API.md`; open an issue if you need them.
• The default limit is 120 list requests a minute per IP. Need more? Run your own Morphit node.
• `/v1/instances` lists other Morphit sites. They all read the same Blurt chain, so their orderbooks largely match (an operator can switch some coins off).
• TypeScript types for the responses are in `packages/indexer-client`.
• To import Morphit's 12-word seed phrases, see `docs/SEED-IMPORT-FOR-WALLET-DEVELOPERS.md`.

Morphit's code is AGPL-3.0. Questions? Join `#agorise:matrix.org` or open an issue at git.agorise.net/agorise/morphit.

---

## How do I get people to use Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `how_to_spread_morphit`

Word of mouth. Every person you bring makes the orderbook more useful for everyone. Ideas that cost little or nothing:

• **Write about it** on Blurt.blog, your own blog or Substack, and share it where it's on-topic.
• **Demo it at meetups** — Bitcoin, Monero, privacy, freedom-tech and agorist groups. Five minutes is enough.
• **Print flyers and stickers** with a big QR code to your site and one line, like "Buy crypto, no ID". Try community boards, cafés, libraries, campuses and factory gates at shift change.
• **Reach other coin communities.** Morphit supports Ethereum, Solana, XRP, Pirate Chain, Decred and more — "trade your coin person to person, no KYC" lands well.
• **Operators:** pay a local promoter a small salary plus bonuses in BLURT for new signups, first trades or demos.

**Don't:**
• Spam groups you're not part of — it burns the name.
• Pitch people happy with their exchange. Pitch the unbanked, the privacy-minded and people whose accounts got frozen.
• Overpromise. Morphit has no escrow, no referee and no guaranteed buyers.

Orders posted on one Morphit site show up on the other Morphit sites too, so local growth helps everyone.

---

## What is two-factor authentication and how do I enable it on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `totp_2fa_what_is_it`

Two-factor authentication (2FA) means unlocking your account in Morphit takes two things: your password, plus a 6-digit code from an app on your phone. The code changes every 30 seconds and can't be used twice while the page is open.

It's optional. Morphit will never force it on you or nag you about it.

To turn it on, go to Settings → Two-factor authentication (2FA) → **Set up 2FA**. Install an open-source authenticator app (we suggest Aegis, 2FAS or Ente Auth), scan the QR code, type the code the app shows, and save your 10 backup codes somewhere safe. The option is there when your account is saved on this device with a password.

Honest limits: 2FA is a lock inside the app, not extra encryption. It stops someone who learned your password from unlocking your account in Morphit. But the 2FA secret sits in the same encrypted file as your keys, so someone with that file AND your password could open it with other software. For a factor that is never in that file, use a YubiKey in YubiKey-only mode (Settings → Hardware key).

---

## I lost my authenticator app — how do I get back in?

**FAQ key:** `totp_2fa_lost_authenticator`

Use a backup code. When you set up 2FA, Morphit gave you 10 backup codes (they look like `XXXX-XXXX`). On the unlock screen, type one where it asks for the 6-digit code — the box takes either. Each backup code works once; Morphit marks it used.

No backup codes left? Sign in again with your 12-word seed phrase: on the unlock screen choose **Sign in with seed phrase**, type the 12 words and choose a new password. Your keys come from the seed, so you get everything back. 2FA is off after that; you can set it up again. (If you joined with an existing Blurt account, you have no seed — use the **Blurt posting key** option instead.)

Nobody can reset 2FA for you. Morphit never holds your keys, so if you lose the authenticator, the backup codes AND the seed, the account can't be recovered.

---

## Why doesn't Morphit recommend Google Authenticator?

**FAQ key:** `totp_2fa_why_not_google_authenticator`

Two reasons:

• **Closed source.** Nobody outside Google can check what it does with your 2FA secrets.
• **Cloud sync.** It backs up your 2FA secrets to your Google account by default (you have to opt out), and they aren't end-to-end encrypted with a password only you know. Anyone who takes over your Google account could get all your codes at once — which defeats the point of a *second*, separate factor.

Morphit suggests open-source apps where you decide where backups go: **Aegis** (Android, encrypted local backups), **2FAS** (iOS and Android, cloud backup only if you turn it on) or **Ente Auth** (every platform, end-to-end encrypted sync).

Already use another authenticator you trust, such as KeePassXC or Bitwarden Authenticator? That's fine. Our list is a suggestion for new users, not a ban.

---

## How does Morphit keep my privacy-coin trades private?

**FAQ key:** `privacy_coins_onchain`

Morphit trades several privacy coins — XMR, DASH, ZEC, ARRR, and DCR — and protects them all the same way.

**Your coins never touch Morphit's chain.** You send them straight from your wallet to your trade partner's, on that coin's own network. The Blurt chain Morphit uses carries only the public listing, your encrypted chat, any listing fee paid in BLURT and, if you leave one, your public review.

**What a listing shows.** A listing is an ad, so its side (buy or sell), coin, currency, price, amount range, payment methods, region (if you set one) and terms are public — that's how people find it. Nothing extra is added: the listing's ID is a random code (`order-…`) that doesn't name the coin, the expiry is rounded down to the day, and no IP address, time zone or browser details are attached. It does carry the language you choose and the tag of the site you post from.

**Amount jitter.** When you share a receive amount in chat, Morphit adds a tiny random amount so the payment can't be matched to your listing by its size. It's on by default.

**Listing fees.** You pay in BLURT (the default), or in BTC or XMR where the site accepts them — never in ZEC, ARRR, DASH or DCR, so their transaction IDs never appear on the Blurt chain. If you pay in XMR, that fee payment's transaction ID and key are written into your listing. Want no Monero link at all? Pay in BLURT; at the base rate it is also half the price.

Each coin has its own [privacy guide](/privacy) — for example [Monero](/privacy/xmr).

---

## What is Barter on Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_barter`

Barter lets you buy or sell goods and services — baskets, bike repairs, a crate of oranges — and settle in crypto.

**How it works:**
• Describe exactly what you're offering in the Terms (required).
• Set its value in your local currency — one price or a range.
• Tick the crypto(s) you'll accept, say XMR, BTC and DOGE. It's **one listing**, not one per coin.

When you and the buyer settle up in chat, Morphit only lets you share a payment address or report a payment in the coins the listing accepts.

**Goods change hands outside Morphit** — in person or by post — and Morphit never touches the goods or the payment. Meet in a public place, share only what you need to, and treat a stranger like a stranger.

Barter is for trading wares only: you can't use it to pay Morphit's listing fee.

---

## What is a Transaction ID (or Hash)?

**FAQ key:** `what_is_a_txid`

When you send crypto, the blockchain gives that payment a unique ID called the Transaction ID. Wallets name it differently: “TxID”, “Transaction Hash”, “Tx Hash” or just “Hash” (Mycelium, for example, calls it “Hash”). It's a long string of letters and numbers, usually 64 characters (Blurt's are 40).

To find it: open your wallet, tap the payment you sent, and copy the ID or Hash it shows.

Pasting it into Morphit lets your trade partner — or, for a listing fee, Morphit — check that the payment really happened.

Anyone with the ID can look the payment up on a public block explorer. On open chains like Bitcoin that shows the amounts and addresses involved; on Monero it shows very little.

---

## Does anything see or leak my IP address when I use Morphit?

**FAQ key:** `ip_address_and_rpc_nodes`

**What this site sees.** Like any website, the server gets your IP address with each request. The code keeps it only in memory, for rate limits — about a minute for ordinary requests, up to 24 hours for the signup limits — and never writes it to disk or a log, or sends it anywhere. The web server keeps addresses only in memory for its own limits and short bans, and keeps no access log with them. No cookies, analytics, trackers or telemetry. Orders, encrypted chat, balances and the block explorer data are all secured on-chain.

**The one possible IP leak.** At most once a day (and once after each site update, or when you press **Try again** on a fee panel), your browser asks a public network node — a Blurt RPC node run by someone else — for the signed release record that says which Morphit version is current. That is two small requests to one node (each may come with a CORS preflight): the last 100 entries of @morphit's history, then the block holding the release. Only if that node fails, sends a record that can't be verified, or names a different release than this site runs, is another node asked the same. If the release is older than those 100 entries, one more history request is made (up to about 115 KB). The result is remembered for 24 hours and shared by all your tabs; if a node offers only a release older than this site's, your browser asks again within the hour. If your browser blocks this site's storage, it can't remember, so it asks each time you open Morphit. You can watch all of it in your browser's Network tab.

**Which nodes.** On an https or plain-http clearnet address: the five public clearnet nodes. On a .onion address: only the seven .onion nodes. On an .i2p address: only the seven .b32.i2p nodes.

**Why.** The record names the current release, Morphit's fee addresses and the fingerprints of the app's start-up files, and it must carry @morphit's signature. A bad node can make the check fail or delay an update notice, but can't fake a release. It catches an outdated or damaged build — not an operator who deliberately serves altered code, since that operator also serves the check.

**What a node learns.** Your IP address, this site's address (on .onion or .i2p, that hidden address), your browser's User-Agent and language, and that someone asked for @morphit's release history. Not your username, orders, chat or balances.

**Use Tor or a VPN** and this is closed: both hide your IP from the nodes and from your operator.
